# Six of the vntr reverse primers begin with a 5' G that the genome does not carry, so five of
# them report one primer mismatch and the sixth, vntr19, happens to match. The primers are kept
# as published, and the published reference sizes already include that base.
# patterns are filled only for the eight loci where the repeat motif published by Van Ert et
# al. 2007 occurs in the reference exactly the published number of times, so that the tandem
# array cross-check is active on them. The source table gives no motifs, so the rest are N/A
# and their alleles rest on amplicon length alone, which is how this panel is numbered. Two
# loci are deliberately left without a pattern although a motif is known for them, because the
# count disagrees with the published value: the pXO2-at array is ten TA units but the panel
# numbers the reference 9, and the vntr16 array is 20 published units of ACATTTAC of which only
# four are perfect copies. An allele in this panel is therefore not always a literal count of
# vrrB1 and vrrB2 have 20 and 13 units of 9 bp in a 229 and a 153 bp product, which leaves 49
# and 36 bp outside the array, less than their two primers occupy. Their primers therefore sit
# inside the repeat array, as happens in other published schemes; the allele formula is
# unaffected because it needs only the size and the copy number to be consistent.
